resources.string: Ondo is a player: it shows the movies, series and channels of the subscription your provider gives you, and provides no content of its own.\n\nTo add your subscription, open Settings, Add playlist: an M3U link or file, or an Xtream Codes login (server address, user name and password). Tap a playlist in Settings to switch to it.

Many providers start category names with a code such as |PT| or FR:. The filter button on Movies, Series and Live TV (also in Settings, Languages and categories) hides a whole language or country at once, in every playlist; the categories the provider adds later follow the same rule.

Styles work the same way with the words of category names: hide Manga & anime, Children or Documentaries, or a word of your own such as Bollywood. Only category names count, not the genre of each movie.

You can also hide categories one by one there, and show them again at any time.
When a stream does not play

Ondo says whether the provider, the network or the format is at fault.

If the provider refuses the stream, the subscription may have expired or too many devices may be watching at once: most providers allow one or two streams at a time.

If the server cannot be reached, check your connection and try again.
Ondo has no account, no ads and no analytics of its own. Your playlists, history and settings stay on your device and are left out of device backups.\n\nOndo connects only to the servers you add.

Add to or remove from My List
In Live TV, long-press a channel to add it to My List.
Use My List on a movie or series page to find it here.

On a movie or series page, My List keeps it at hand. In Live TV, long-press a channel to add it to My List.

The My List tab gathers your movies, series and channels; search is the magnifying glass at the top of each screen.

Collections are your own groups, such as Weekend or Kids: use Collection on a movie or series page, then find them in My List, under Collections.

Movies, Series and Live TV show your provider’s categories. Search, the magnifying glass at the top of each screen, looks through channels, movies and series. In Search, the filter button keeps the movies and series released in the years you choose, or the movies of a festival or ceremony.\n\nIn a category, the sort button orders the posters by playlist order, name, date added, release date or rating. Movie pages show their awards and festival selections. Tap the name of a director or an actor on a movie or series page to see their other movies and series among the pages you have opened. Genres, the year and awards open the titles of your playlist that share them the same way. Search also finds actors and directors by name.

The guide button on Live TV shows the programmes of the channels chosen there (My List, a category or all of them). The guide comes from your provider, or from the XMLTV address given when adding an M3U playlist.\n\nOpen an upcoming programme and set a reminder: a notification arrives a few minutes before it starts. The bell of the guide lists your reminders.
